sec: HCV progression, acute disease, serology and interpretation, SVR, drugs and extrahepatic disease

items.q: Progression chain — match — 1) After infection 2) Acute phase 3) Chronic phase 4) End stage … A) Chance for chronic hepatitis B) Cirrhosis / liver failure / portal hypertension C) HCC D) Incubation period of about 50 days
items.exp: 'Incubation period : 50 days → Acute → Chance for chronic → Cirrhosis / Liver failure (PHTN) → HCC'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Judge the acute phase: I Acute HCV is usually anicteric and therefore usually undiagnosed. II Enzymes are variable and fulminant failure occurs in 0.1 – 1%.
items.exp: 'Acute : Anicteric hepatitis, usually undiagnosed; Enzymes : variable; Fulminant failure : 0.1-1%'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Risk of fulminant hepatic failure printed for acute HCV?
Serology — match the marker to the window — 1) Earliest marker after infection 2) Appears after the serological window … A) Anti-HCV B) HCV RNA
items.exp: The window phase shows HCV RNA first, with anti-HCV appearing later ('Serologic window', 'HCV RNA', 'Anti-HCV' sequence). (Book p1046)

items.q: An immunosuppressed patient (CKD / haemodialysis / HIV) has a negative anti-HCV EIA. What does this page advise?
opts: Test HCV RNA, because such patients may not produce anti-HCV
No further testing is needed — the patient is not infected
Do a liver biopsy to rule out cirrhosis
items.exp: 'CKD / Hemodialysis / HIV (Immunosuppressed patients may not produce anti-HCV) → HCV RNA'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Interpretation of anti-HCV EIA — match — 1) Positive 2) Negative … A) No HCV contact B) Acute / chronic infection or recovered
items.exp: '+ve → acute / chronic infection / recovered'; '-ve → No HCV contact'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Which investigation is printed to rule out cirrhosis in chronic HCV?
Presentation — match — 1) Acute HCV 2) Chronic HCV … A) Asymptomatic / extrahepatic manifestations B) Fever, flu-like illness, fatigue
items.exp: 'Acute : Fever / flu like illness, fatigue'; 'Chronic : Asymptomatic / extra hepatic manifestations'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Sustained viral response — match the condition to the printed SVR — 1) Chronic HCV 2) Cirrhosis 3) Decompensated liver disease … A) 60% B) 75% C) 99.5 – 99.7%
items.exp: 'Condition : Chronic HCV / Cirrhosis / Decompensated liver disease; Response (SVR) : 99.5-99.7% / 75 / 60%'. (Book p1046)

items.q: What age threshold does the page print for treating HCV?
opts: Treat anyone above 12 years of age
Treat anyone above 18 years of age
Treat only after fibrosis stage F2

items.q: Regimen — match the DAA class to the drug printed — 1) NS3 2) NS5A 3) NS5B … A) Sofosbuvir B) Velpatasvir C) Glecaprevir / simeprevir
items.exp: 'NS3 (-) : Glecaprevir / simeprevir; NS5A (-) : velpatasvir; NS5B (-) : Sofosbuvir + Ribavirin'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Duration printed for the DAA combination in chronic HCV with cirrhosis?
items.exp: 'Combination for 12 weeks for chronic HCV with cirrhosis'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Which DAA component is flagged as not available in India on this page?
items.exp: 'Not available in India' is printed against the NS5A agent velpatasvir. (Book p1046)

items.q: Which is NOT one of the printed extrahepatic manifestations of HCV?
items.exp: Printed list: Sjogren's syndrome, extranodal B-cell marginal zone lymphoma, essential mixed cryoglobulinaemia, porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, MPGN, autoimmune thyroid illness. (Book p1046)

items.q: Extrahepatic manifestations — match — 1) Essential mixed cryoglobulinaemia 2) Extranodal marginal zone lymphoma 3) Renal lesion … A) Salivary gland B) Classical MPGN C) Type 2 and type 3
items.exp: 'Essential mixed cryoglobulinemia type 2, 3'; 'extranodal B cell marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) : salivary gland'; 'Classical MPGN (membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis)'. (Book p1046)

items.q: Which thyroid disease is printed among the extrahepatic associations of HCV?
What is the printed treatment headline for chronic HCV drugs?
opts: New DAAs, pangenotypic drugs with markedly improved SVR
items.exp: 'Drugs : New DAAs, pangenomic drugs with ↑↑ SVR'. (Book p1046)
